method: Rasterise saved body lines at 288 dpi; measure rows containing at least two dark pixels (all RGB channels below 120). Compare with font size stored in the same PDF. This calibrates ink, not legibility of new handwriting.

samples.text: Panel one. Pip the Fox, with orange fur, round glasses, a green hoodie with a yellow lightning patch,
and red high-top sneakers, shuts the bedroom door with a BANG. The blue sketchbook stays
tucked under one arm. Pip drops onto the bed. Everyone is annoying, Pip thinks, and that is all Pip
Panel two. A warm orange caption box floats over Pip's head. The word in it is EXACT. Pip squints
through the round glasses and reads the box slowly, one line at a time.
"Think of one small thing that bugged you this week. Say the first word that comes. Probably bad,
or mad. Now find a sharper word. Annoyed? Embarrassed? Left out? Let down? Jealous? Nervous?
Pick one. If two fit, say both. Say it out loud: 'I felt embarrassed, and a bit annoyed.' Now give it a
number from 1 to 10. That's it. The word is a tool, not a grade."
Panel three. Pip sighs. The first word that comes is not very exact. Pip draws it as a giant hat in the
margin of the sketchbook. It is labelled BAD, and it is a hat that fits every head and no head. Pip
Pip tries again and looks for a sharper word. Pip picks one that fits, or two if two fit, and says it out

use: Review reference only. Unreadable readback and measured clipping remain stops. No font size inferred from tight drawn ink boxes.
